clue.text: At sea, leaving opening for sailor?

definitions.text: At sea, leaving opening for sailor?

indicators.note: opening for means making room for, so the jumbled word parts to take in the sailor
at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters of leaving are jumbled

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone is all at sea, abandoning a job vacancy meant for a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' shuffles LEAVING (giving NAVIGLE), which is 'opening for' AB. The whole clue also describes the answer: waters at sea that leave an opening for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that can be sailed through by ships, leaving a clear passage, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Volume penned by Fielding?

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the comedian's first name wraps round the volume letter

parts.note: Noel Fielding is a British comedian, of The Mighty Boosh and Bake Off

explanation.surface: A query about a book written by Henry Fielding, the eighteenth-century author.
explanation.walkthrough: Fielding suggests Henry Fielding, author of Tom Jones, which makes the whole clue a definition; for the wordplay, it is the comedian Noel Fielding.
explanation.definitionFit: A book-length work of prose fiction, the form Henry Fielding helped to establish in English.

clue.text: Six books date from one year

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
a date or period in history can be called an age

explanation.surface: Six volumes are dated to a single year, like a bibliographer's catalogue entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine described this way comes from the harvest of a single specified year.

clue.text: So walls go around cavity insulation

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of 'So walls go' are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A builder's note: the walls are wrapped in insulation for the cavity.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibrous material spun from molten glass is packed into wall cavities and lofts to keep heat in.

clue.text: Favourite early Sinatra?

definitions.meaning: a person's pet or darling, the one who can do no wrong
Frank Sinatra was nicknamed Ol' Blue Eyes, so as a youngster he was a lad with eyes of that colour

explanation.surface: A fan names their favourite as the young Frank Sinatra.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a favoured person who is indulged by those in charge, a pet or golden child.

clue.text: So many footballers in Germany little help at Christmas

definitions.meaning: a football team has eleven players, and the German word for eleven is spelt this way
one of Santa's small helpers in the workshop

explanation.surface: German football squads apparently offer little help over the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: German for the number eleven, the size of a football team, and also Santa's small workshop helper.

clue.text: Naked, Lucy puts on revolutionary total moisturiser

indicators.note: puts on as in dons clothing: the middle of Lucy is wrapped in the other piece
revolutionary means turning round, so the word for a total is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is a total

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer covering, so Lucy loses her first and last letters

explanation.surface: Lucy, unclothed, applies a whole pot of a revolutionary skin cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts on' reads as applying cream, but it means wearing, the reversed total wrapped round the middle of Lucy.
explanation.definitionFit: The slimy secretion of the body's membranes keeps them moist, a humorous take on a skin product.

clue.text: One interrupts chairman with example from Pet Sounds

indicators.note: interrupts means breaks into, so the letter for one goes inside the chairman

parts.note: Mao Zedong was known as Chairman Mao
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cut-in on the chairman with a track from the Beach Boys' album Pet Sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Pet Sounds is the Beach Boys album, but here it means noises made by pets.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's cry is one of the noises domestic animals make.

clue.text: A short stay in cold hospital, to cure this?

definitions.text: A short stay in cold hospital, to cure this?

indicators.note: in places the shortened stay within the letters for cold and hospital

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the word for stay loses its last letter

parts.note: to tarry is to stay or linger

explanation.surface: Would a brief stay in a chilly hospital cure this complaint?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the ailment, a congested nose that a short stay in hospital might cure; the parse inserts without a separate indicator, the clue's 'in' doing the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A build-up of phlegm in the nose and throat is the complaint a stay might treat.

clue.text: Wrong filling for tusk that's trouble for cavities

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: the filling of a word is its inside, so tusk gives up its middle letters

parts.note: that's expands to 'it is', written as one run

explanation.surface: A dentist's verdict: the wrong filling was put in a tusk, causing cavity trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The cavities are the hollows in the skull behind the nose, not holes in teeth, despite 'filling' and 'tusk'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the air-filled hollows in the facial bones is a common complaint.

clue.text: State's little advantage for everyone at university

parts.note: van is a short form of advantage (vantage) in tennis scoring
U is the British film certificate for films suitable for all
taken as written

explanation.surface: A government gives a slight edge to every student at university.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pacific island nation is a sovereign country; the definition reads as 'the state is'.

clue.text: Floor below apartment 11?

definitions.meaning: to floor is to knock down or level
the apartment numbered one lower than eleven would be the tenth one, written as two words

explanation.surface: A query about the storey beneath apartment 11.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor an opponent is to knock them down level, to lay them out on the ground.

clue.text: Many young men bringing in nothing

indicators.note: bringing in means taking something inside, so the zero goes into the young men

parts.note: lads are young men
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Plenty of youths come along empty-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a great quantity or a large number, as in heaps or lots.

clue.text: Boxing minor asset transported to China?

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the scrambled asset holds the minor inside
transported means carried off and moved about, so the letters of asset are rearranged

parts.note: a ward is a minor in the care of a guardian

explanation.surface: A young boxer, a valuable asset, is shipped off to China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' rearranges asset into EASTS; 'Boxing' is the container, not a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: From Europe, China lies in the direction of the sunrise, so heading there means travelling that way.

clue.text: List of acts forced to busk to eat

indicators.note: forced means wrenched out of shape, so the letters of 'to busk to eat' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of street performers forced to busk to earn food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List of acts' looks like a variety bill, but the acts are Acts of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of laws passed by a legislature is the record of its Acts.

clue.text: Situation for a man with iron balls?

definitions.text: Situation for a man with iron balls?

parts.words: Situation for a man with iron balls?
parts.note: a golfer carries irons, and the position in which a golf ball comes to rest decides the next shot

explanation.surface: What predicament awaits a man of steely courage?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron balls' suggests nerve, but the man is a golfer: iron is a club and balls are what he hits.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the word names the position where a ball has come to rest.

clue.text: Did corrupt US lawyers rent out houses with little light?

indicators.note: houses means holds within, so the word for rent out encloses the lawyers

parts.note: to let a flat is to rent it out
DAs are district attorneys, American prosecutors
a ray is a thin beam, a small amount of light

explanation.surface: Crooked American lawyers rent out dimly lit properties.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone off the right path is to corrupt them morally, here in the past tense.

clue.text: Clear out around pigsty with mum

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for out goes about the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
a pen is an enclosure for animals such as pigs
and means with
mum as in keep mum, be quiet: sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone cleans out the pigsty, helped by their mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A case so obvious that it is settled at once is perfectly plain.

clue.text: One absent after duel goes wrong

indicators.note: goes wrong means comes apart from its proper form, so the letters of 'after duel' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somebody goes missing after a duel ends badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier absent without leave, or someone failing to turn up or pay, is one who has defaulted.

clue.text: Spitting Image fan entertains large kid with the truth

parts.note: a spitting image is an exact lookalike, a double

indicators.note: entertains means hosts as a guest, so the fan holds the large letter inside

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or fan
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: A fan of the satirical TV puppet show Spitting Image has a big goat over.
explanation.walkthrough: Spitting Image was a British TV satire using puppets; here it simply means a lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: This ploy deceives by telling the truth while expecting not to be believed, to kid someone.

clue.text: Disparate states working together a fiction king feeds

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is a body of states cooperating

indicators.note: feeds means goes into, so the king is put inside the fiction

parts.note: a lie is a fiction
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Dissimilar countries cooperate, fed by a story about a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are different and dissimilar can be described with this old-fashioned word.

clue.text: Ambrose regularly ignored wife

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter is skipped, so only alternate letters of Ambrose survive

explanation.surface: A man named Ambrose kept neglecting his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The title used for a married woman stands for the woman herself, as in 'the missus'.

clue.text: Cake boxed up in varied amounts

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
boxed means contained, so the letters sit inside 'varied amounts'

explanation.surface: A cake packed into boxes in assorted quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxed' points to ARIEDAM inside 'varied amounts'; 'up' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain sponge traditionally eaten with a glass of the Portuguese fortified wine.

clue.text: Undesirable corporation let Middle Eastern city stand

definitions.meaning: corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, so this is unwanted flab round the waist
to spare the Lebanese port of Tyre would be to let it stand rather than destroy it

explanation.surface: An unwelcome company decides a Middle Eastern city may remain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is a dated humorous word for a paunch, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll of fat around the middle is jokingly likened to the extra wheel carried in a car.

clue.text: Correct objective in Middle East? On the contrary

indicators.note: in places one piece within another, here the region within the objective
on the contrary reverses which piece holds which, so the objective goes round the region

parts.note: an end is an objective or aim

explanation.surface: A query about the right aim for policy in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, the objective would go inside the region; 'On the contrary' flips which piece holds which.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise a text by removing its errors is to put it right.

clue.text: Jack leaves shake that contains unpasteurised milk

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the letter for Jack goes from the word for shake

parts.note: to judder is to shake or vibrate
J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards

explanation.surface: Jack walks out of a milkshake bar selling raw milk.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow's milk gland holds the milk straight from the animal, before any heat treatment.

clue.text: Switch carpet again

definitions.meaning: an electrically operated switch used in circuits
to put a floor covering down once more

explanation.surface: Swap the carpet for a fresh one.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical switch worked by a small current, and also to lay something down a second time.

clue.text: Ten suspiciously following one in sheep's clothing

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the rearranged ten goes at the end
in means placed within, so the letter for one goes inside the sheep

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: suspiciously means in a shady, crooked way, so the letters of ten are jumbled

explanation.surface: Ten suspicious characters trail a wolf in sheep's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspiciously' rearranges ten into ENT. 'sheep's clothing' reads as one phrase, but the clothing is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for garments or attire.

clue.text: Rugby lad's annual fitness test given up

indicators.note: in a down clue, given up means sent upwards, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the MOT is the yearly roadworthiness test for British cars

explanation.surface: A rugby player abandons his yearly fitness assessment.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's compulsory annual check that a car is roadworthy. Rugby is the school, not the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Brown is the boy hero of Tom Brown's School Days, set at Rugby School; the definition reads as 'the lad is'.

clue.text: Ornithologist finally returned nest, after leg up

indicators.note: after means following, so the later pieces come behind the leg side

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of ornithologist
returned means sent back, so the word for nest is read backwards

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den or nest

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher brings a nest back after a leg-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg and on are the same side of a cricket field. 'returned' turns LAIR into RIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone up before the court is facing trial.

clue.text: Competitors with yen for fresh start give up the fight

indicators.note: for fresh start means the opening letter is swapped for a new one

parts.note: the field is all the competitors in a race
Y is the symbol for the Japanese currency yen

explanation.surface: Contestants hungry for a new beginning throw in the towel.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede or surrender is to stop resisting an opponent.

clue.text: Graduate entry requirement includes study plan

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so the word for study goes inside the entry requirement

parts.note: a key is needed to get in
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A graduate admissions rule that includes a programme of study.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare is to plan and arrange things in advance.
